title: Brrr It's Cold: Why Do We Shiver and Chattering Teeth?

lines.text: Brrr, brrr, blow the winter wind, wrap your scarf up to your chin!
lines.caps: *BRRR, brrr, blow the winter *WIND, | wrap your scarf up to your *CHIN!

lines.text: Why do our muscles shake and our teeth go clack-clack-clack when we feel chilly?
lines.caps: Why do our muscles *SHAKE | and our teeth go clack-clack-clack *WHEN | we feel *CHILLY?

lines.text: Shivering is your body's built-in emergency heating furnace!
lines.caps: Shivering is your body's *BUILT-IN | emergency heating *FURNACE!

lines.text: When tiny thermometers in your skin feel the cold, your brain sends an instant alert!
lines.caps: When tiny thermometers in your *SKIN | feel the cold, your brain sends an *INSTANT | *ALERT!

lines.text: Your brain commands skeletal muscles to twitch and tighten up to thirty times a second!
lines.caps: Your brain commands skeletal *MUSCLES | to twitch and tighten up to thirty times a *SECOND!

lines.text: Rapid muscle movement burns stored glucose energy and releases warm thermal heat!
lines.caps: Rapid muscle movement burns *STORED | glucose energy and releases warm *THERMAL | *HEAT!

lines.text: Your jaw muscles contract too, making your teeth chatter together!
lines.caps: Your jaw muscles *CONTRACT | too, making your teeth *CHATTER | *TOGETHER!

lines.text: Shivering quickly warms your core back up to a toasty ninety-eight degrees!
lines.caps: Shivering quickly warms your *CORE | back up to a toasty ninety-eight *DEGREES!

lines.text: Warm up with smart science—subscribe to BabyBeats Rhymo!
